newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Pepsi making slow comeback in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi making slow comeback in Venezuela.

text.p: U.S. soft drinks giant PepsiCo has slowly regained a toehold in the Venezuelan market it dominated a year ago, although it has still not recovered its national distribution network, a top company official said.

Pepsi, which until the defection of its local bottler to chief rival Coca-Cola last August held an 80 percent of the market, is now selling about two million cases per month, Ramon Viso, Pepsi's marketing manager in Venezuela told Reuters.
Coca-Cola and Pepsi executives have said previously that the Venezuelan soft drinks market would total about 200 million cases in 1997.

After losing its 50-year-old franchise partnership with the country's leading bottler, Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras de Venezuela, Pepsi was left without a bottling and distribution network and virtually disappeared from the market.
Although Venezuela contributed only 0.6 percent of company profits, the move stung Pepsi.
After a failed legal battle challenging the surprise switch, Pepsi signed a 30/70 joint venture with leading foods and beverage company Polar in November.
Viso said the partnership with Polar now had distribution in 60 percent of the country and that in some parts of the country, particularly in Caracas, it was outselling its rival.
"Where we have our product we are five percentage points ahead," he said.
The Coca-Cola and Cisneros joint venture in Venezuela was bought out by Mexico-based bottling giant Panamerican Beverages Inc for $100 million in cash and about 30.6 million in shares.
